bronze_male.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Workout Tracker sport mastery avatar. Generate exactly ONE fictional male Tennis athlete for the Bronze tier. Polished premium semi-realistic stylised 3D game-skin illustration, credible for ages 10 through adult; crisp face, natural athletic proportions, well-defined hands and believable equipment. Original character, not a real athlete or celebrity. Character identity: light warm skin, short sandy brown hair, hazel eyes. Visibly junior athlete, approximately 12–14, natural youthful face and proportions, modest practical kit; no adult musculature or jewellery. Collection palette: white/light-blue junior kit; navy/white premium kit; restrained gold final accents. This tier's outfit below determines the current colours. Outfit: Simple junior white/light-blue shirt and shorts, basic racket and shoes. Equipment: One correctly strung tennis racket with a long handle and yellow tennis ball. Practical tennis shoes. Female uses athletic shorts or a functional tennis skirt with suitable coverage; equal kit quality. Award: None. Pose: Standing with racket head angled down, ball held in free hand. Tier silhouette direction: Relaxed introductory three-quarter view; natural asymmetrical weight distribution and curious expression. Establish the junior identity without a stiff catalogue stance. Square portrait. Entire head, hands, equipment and both feet visible, centred with 6–8% clear transparent margins. Athlete occupies roughly 80–88% of canvas height; trophies fit naturally inside the frame. Keep face and torso unobstructed. Match the rendering finish and proportions of the supplied style reference, but follow this tier's kit and award brief. Keep the corresponding male and female tier equal in prestige, award scale, kit quality and visual presence. Create a real transparent background with clean alpha edges. No words, lettering, numbers, brand or team logos, watermark, border, background scene, extra people, unrelated weapons, fantasy armour, wings, magic, neon aura or trophy clutter. Bronze has no award. Do not invent extra medals or accessories. No copied official trophy inscriptions. Preserve recognisable eye shape, skin tone and hair character, while visibly ageing the same fictional person. Do not preserve the junior face proportions in adult tiers. Mature facial structure, natural eye-to-face proportions, a developed nose/jaw and less rounded cheeks must make Platinum onward unmistakably adult in BOTH appearances; do not rely on muscles, makeup, a beard, suit or trophies to signal age. Styling stays polished and semi-realistic, with no oversized doll eyes or baby-faced adult. Pose references supply equipment/kit only: do not duplicate their stance, hand placement, body angle or expression across tiers. The sport is this individual's story, not a demographic stereotype or a restriction that this person can only play one sport.

Sport-specific constraints: Grand Slam-level cups and a year-end champion presentation provide the story. There is no invented universally highest tennis trophy. Use original unbranded trophy silhouettes and neutral ribbons.
Input is STYLE ONLY, do not copy its character. Distinct fictional Tennis boy age13, light warm skin, SHORT SANDY BROWN straight hair, HAZEL eyes, slender junior face/natural anatomy. Simple white/light-blue junior shirt/shorts, practical white tennis shoes and short socks. ONE correctly strung long-handle tennis racket held angled downward at side, single yellow tennis ball in free hand. Relaxed asymmetrical three-quarter introduction, no award/accessories. All body/racket/shoes inside square 6–8% clear alpha margins.
